pathway.title: American Airlines Group Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The earnings and leverage profile is weak and still deteriorating: EBITDA calculated from statement lines fell to USD 2,891 million over the last twelve months from USD 4,970 million in FY2023 while revenue grew 15.52%, so the EBITDA margin fell from 9.42% to 4.74% and total debt reached 10.25x EBITDA. Net debt fell 15.70% over the same period, which shows cash building and not earnings recovery. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Fuel is the transmission channel and it is unhedged: in the nine months to September 2026 fuel cost rose by USD 4,427 million, absorbing 69.74% of the USD 6,348 million revenue gain, and each ten cents per gallon adds about USD 450 million, or 15.57% of last-twelve-months EBITDA, so fuel at the third-quarter level erodes coverage faster than fares can reprice. Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45, 69

- Cash generation does not fund investment from earnings: capital spending of USD 4,358 million was 1.51x EBITDA and free cash flow was negative USD 91 million, because operating cash flow of USD 4,267 million was lifted by USD 2,970 million of working capital and other items, and customer-funded float supplied 70.60% of nine-month operating cash flow, which reverses if bookings weaken. Basis: calculation C7; calculation C8; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Liquidity is the genuine support but it is not unlimited: USD 11,797 million, including USD 3,510 million of undrawn facilities, covers 0.98x of the principal due through 2028 and 60.78% of that principal plus aircraft and engine commitments, so the debt service plan depends on continued financing as well as on cash on hand. Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 60–61, 64–66

- Refinancing capacity is demonstrated but secured: in 2026 the company extended revolvers to 2031 and term loans to 2033 and raised USD 4,102 million of aircraft and engine debt, yet 87.22% of principal is secured, 52.24% sits in aircraft certificates and loyalty financing, and a USD 7,861 million maturity falls in 2028. Basis: calculation C9; calculation C13; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Financial policy and governance are supportive but unverified: there is no sponsor, no dividend or buyback, and audited reporting, while American Airlines, Inc. holds a USD 12,512 million net receivable from the parent and board and ownership detail was not supplied, so governance risk stays medium. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

- The business model supports revenue but not margin: loyalty is 13.81% of revenue and yield rose 12.1%, yet unit cost growth of 12.5% outran unit revenue growth of 10.9%, salaries rose USD 962 million, most employees are unionised and regional capacity contracts commit USD 4,461 million of minimum payments. Basis: calculation C11; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48, 66; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Claims outside the debt figure add to the burden: operating lease liabilities of USD 6,639 million equal 22.40% of total debt, aircraft and engine commitments are USD 24,056 million, and the accident and antitrust litigation is not sized, so leverage understates the fixed claims on cash. Basis: calculation C17; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

cells.text: American Airlines Group Inc. is a holding company whose main business is a major network air carrier with nine hubs (Charlotte, Chicago, Dallas/Fort Worth, Los Angeles, Miami, New York, Philadelphia, Phoenix and Washington, D.C.), service to over 350 destinations and about 224 million passengers boarded in 2025.

Principal wholly-owned subsidiaries are American Airlines, Inc., Envoy Aviation Group Inc., PSA Airlines, Inc. and Piedmont Airlines, Inc.; the group reports one operating segment that includes the loyalty program.

FY2025 operating revenues were USD 54,633 million: passenger travel 83.48%, loyalty travel 7.39%, loyalty marketing services 6.43%, cargo 1.54% and other 1.17% (calculation C1). Nine months 2026 were USD 46,982 million with the same shape (calculation C2).
Domestic flights were 70.91% of FY2025 passenger revenue and 70.89% in nine months 2026; Atlantic, Latin America and Pacific make up the rest (calculation C4).

AAdvantage is described as a material asset: loyalty revenue was 13.81% of FY2025 revenue, partner cash payments were USD 6.2 billion in 2025 and USD 6.1 billion in 2024, Citibank N.A. became exclusive U.S. co-brand card issuer in 2026, and the loyalty program liability was USD 11,514 million at 2026-09-30.

567 regional aircraft fly as American Eagle under capacity purchase agreements in which American keeps all revenue and pays predetermined fees; 396 are flown by wholly-owned carriers and 171 by third-party carriers (Republic and SkyWest).
The mainline fleet was 1,013 aircraft at 2025-12-31, of which 547 were owned and 466 leased, with an average age of 14.3 years; commitments cover 383 new aircraft at 2025-12-31 and 365 at 2026-09-30.
No fuel hedges are held and policy is not to hedge; fuel was 20% of FY2025 operating expenses at USD 2.39 per gallon and the 2026 nine-month average price was USD 3.58 per gallon.

About 139,100 full-time equivalent employees at 2025-12-31, approximately 86% represented by unions; pilot (Allied Pilots Association) and TWU-IAM mechanic and fleet service contracts become amendable in 2027 and flight attendant and passenger service contracts in 2029.

Competes with major network, low-cost and ultra-low-cost carriers; founding member of the oneworld Alliance with joint businesses with British Airways, Aer Lingus, Iberia and Finnair, Japan Airlines and Qantas.
Revenue peaks in summer; the air traffic liability was USD 9,414 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 7,158 million at 2025-12-31.
Subject to Department of Transportation, Federal Aviation Administration and antitrust oversight; non-U.S. citizens are capped at 24.9% of votes and 49.0% of equity.
Third quarter 2026 revenue was USD 16,335 million, up 19.3%; fuel USD 4,635 million, up 67.5%; operating income USD 115 million against USD 151 million; net loss USD 269 million.

runs.text: The five strongest supports all work through cash availability rather than earnings. Liquidity of USD 11,797 million, with revolvers maturing in 2031 and term loans in 2033, gives the company time to absorb a fuel shock without a near-term maturity, which lowers the probability of a liquidity-driven default over the next two years even though it does not cover the 2028 wall alone. Loyalty brings partner cash of USD 6.2 billion in 2025 and 13.81% of revenue, which both supports unit revenue and gives lenders a pledgeable cash stream, although USD 5,985 million of secured debt already draws on it. Scale and network, with nine hubs and a domestic share of 70.89% of passenger revenue, spread demand across markets and let capacity and pricing respond to local conditions. Demonstrated access to asset-backed markets, with USD 4,102 million raised in nine months, lowers refinancing risk for as long as lenders accept aircraft collateral, whose values were not supplied. No dividends or buybacks keep cash in the business, which supports debt service. Basis: calculation C2; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C13; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

The five weaknesses all work through thin earnings against fixed claims. Leverage of 10.25x and cash interest cover of 1.81x leave little room for a further earnings decline, so a modest fall in EBITDA moves both measures materially. Unhedged fuel and rising unit cost turn price shocks directly into lower EBITDA, as the 69.74% absorption of the 2026 revenue gain shows. Free cash flow of negative USD 91 million and dependence on float for 70.60% of nine-month operating cash flow mean the cash position is partly borrowed from customers and will shrink if bookings slow. The maturity profile puts USD 12,042 million of principal, 41.07% of the total, due by 2028, and the secured share of 87.22% limits the assets that can back new debt. Fixed commitments, namely USD 24,056 million of aircraft and engine purchases, USD 4,461 million of regional capacity payments, USD 6,639 million of operating leases and labour contracts that open in 2027, reduce cost flexibility when revenue falls. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C13; calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 64–66

cells.text: American Airlines Group Inc. (AAG, file number 1-8400) and its wholly-owned subsidiary American Airlines, Inc. (American, file number 1-2691) file one combined report.
United States; AAG is a Delaware corporation with principal executive offices at 1 Skyview Drive, Fort Worth, Texas.
Scheduled passenger and cargo air transportation (major network air carrier).
AAG was formed in 1982 as AMR Corporation, parent of American, which was founded in 1934 with roots in a 1926 air mail carrier.
Common stock listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under AAL; large accelerated filer (American Airlines, Inc. is a non-accelerated filer and its stock is not traded).
662,618,434 AAG shares at 2026-10-16 and 1,000 American shares, all held by AAG; 660,304,573 AAG shares at 2026-02-13.

Approximately 51,000 holders of record at 2026-02-13; many shares are held through brokers and the number of beneficial holders is not stated; non-affiliate market value was approximately USD 7.4 billion at 2025-06-30.
None disclosed; holders above 5% are not named because that table is in the proxy statement, which was not supplied.
Signature pages identify twelve directors for AAG, including the Chief Executive Officer and President and a separate Chairman, and the Chief Financial Officer; three directors sign for American.
KPMG LLP, Dallas, Texas, opinion dated 2026-02-18 on the FY2025 statements and internal control.
About 139,100 full-time equivalents at 2025-12-31 and 141,100 at 2026-09-30.
The annual report states a non-investment-grade corporate credit rating and names no agency, level or outlook.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No acquisition, merger, disposal or sponsor transaction appears in the five filings, so the transaction record is a funding one. In the nine months to September 2026 the group raised USD 5,933 million of long-term debt and repaid USD 5,347 million, and principal outstanding rose from USD 28,594 million at the 2025 year end to USD 29,321 million. No equity was issued for cash; the only new shares came from employee plans. Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 14–15

New secured aircraft and engine debt was the largest source: USD 127 million from the last of the 2025 aircraft trusts, USD 1,141 million from the May 2026 trusts, USD 567 million of engine certificates in June, USD 692 million so far from the USD 1.3 billion August trusts, USD 870 million of junior borrowings on aircraft already delivered and USD 705 million of floating-rate equipment loans. These sum to USD 4,102 million and match the roughly USD 4.1 billion the company reports. A further USD 633 million of the August proceeds sat in escrow at 2026-09-30 and is not counted as debt. Basis: calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–20, 45–46

Bank debt was amended rather than replaced. In March 2026 the three revolving facilities were re-established with commitments of about USD 3.1 billion, undrawn, and their maturity moved from June 2029 to March 2031; in May 2026 about USD 1.1 billion of term loans due January 2027 were refinanced into term loans maturing May 2033 at SOFR plus 3.00%, with USD 703 million of incremental borrowings; and in February 2026 the margin on the 2025 AAdvantage term loan was cut to SOFR plus 2.75%. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–17, 45–46; 10-K_2025-12-31_aal_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 198

Repayments were funded from new debt and cash: USD 629 million of short-term term loan, USD 1.0 billion of 8.50% senior secured notes and USD 310 million of aircraft equipment notes were prepaid, alongside USD 2.8 billion of scheduled repayments. After these transactions the aircraft certificate balance is USD 9,332 million, the AAdvantage secured debt is USD 5,985 million, and the Treasury's notes of USD 3,746 million fall due in 2030 and 2031. One subsequent event in October 2026 added purchase options on five Airbus A320 Family aircraft to commitments the company intends to finance with cash and long-term debt. Basis: calculation C8; calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–20, 64–65

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This is the financial foundation for American Airlines Group Inc. as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway. It extracts and normalises the group's statements from two annual and three quarterly reports and builds leverage, coverage, liquidity and maturity figures from them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high and rising: total debt is 10.25x derived EBITDA for the twelve months to September 2026, so creditors rely on USD 11,797 million of liquidity and refinancing rather than earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C8; calculation C6; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The deterioration comes from earnings, not borrowing: derived EBITDA fell from USD 4,970 million in FY2023 to USD 3,357 million in FY2025 while total debt fell from USD 32,902 million to USD 29,007 million, and in the nine months to September 2026 fuel cost rose by USD 4,427 million against revenue growth of USD 6,348 million. EBITDA covered cash interest only 1.81x on the last twelve months, down from 2.28x in FY2023.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C15; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The figures rest on EBITDA calculated from statement lines because the issuer states none, on cash that includes short-term investments, and on quarterly cash flow statements that print operating cash flow as one total. Principal of USD 29,321 million reconciles to carrying value of USD 29,635 million through finance leases of USD 660 million and issuance costs of USD 346 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C10; calculation C3; calculation C1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt to derived EBITDA rose from 6.62x in FY2023 to 6.71x in FY2024, 8.64x in FY2025 and 10.25x for the twelve months to September 2026, and net debt to EBITDA rose from 5.10x to 7.38x. Debt fell by USD 3,895 million between FY2023 and FY2025, so the deterioration comes from earnings: EBITDA fell from USD 4,970 million to USD 3,357 million as salaries, wages and benefits rose by USD 2,986 million while revenue rose by USD 1,845 million. For creditors, debt repayment has been outweighed by weaker operating earnings, which leaves refinancing capacity rather than debt reduction as the main source of comfort.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C8; calculation C17; calculation C1; calculation C2; 10-K_2025-12-31_aal_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 142

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In 2026 the shock is fuel. Aircraft fuel and related taxes rose by USD 4,427 million to USD 12,444 million in the first nine months as the average price per gallon rose from USD 2.38 to USD 3.58, and the issuer states it held no fuel hedging contracts at 30 September 2026, so the increase flowed straight through: operating income fell by USD 494 million to USD 521 million although revenue rose by USD 6,348 million. A further rise in fuel or a slowdown in revenue therefore moves EBITDA, and leverage, directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.28x in FY2023, 2.35x in FY2024, 1.98x in FY2025 and 1.81x for the last twelve months. Cash interest paid fell from USD 2,180 million in FY2023 to USD 1,594 million over the last twelve months, but EBITDA fell faster, so coverage has weakened even as debt service cost fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C8; calculation C6; 10-K_2025-12-31_aal_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 194; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is liquidity and net debt. Cash and short-term investments of USD 8,287 million, against USD 5,836 million at the FY2025 year end, took net debt down from USD 23,171 million to USD 21,348 million even though gross debt rose, so near-term refinancing risk is lower than the leverage multiple implies. The view would improve if EBITDA recovers toward the FY2024 level of USD 4,540 million, and weaken if fuel costs stay at the 2026 level while revenue growth slows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C3; calculation C2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation does not cover investment on a last-twelve-months basis: free cash flow after working capital was a deficit of USD 680 million in FY2025 (operating cash flow of USD 3,099 million less capital expenditures of USD 3,779 million) and a deficit of USD 91 million for the last twelve months. Operating cash flow of USD 4,541 million in the nine months to September 2026 is helped by working capital: air traffic liability rose by USD 2,256 million and loyalty program liability by USD 950 million since the year end, and the issuer attributes the rise in operating cash flow mainly to those increases. This is customer-funded float that unwinds if bookings soften, so operating cash flow overstates the cash the business generates from earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C14; calculation C16; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 61

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditures and aircraft purchase deposits were USD 2,728 million in the nine months to September 2026 against USD 2,149 million a year earlier, and the issuer does not split them into maintenance and growth. With free cash flow near zero on a last-twelve-months basis, net debt reduction depends on float growth and on access to financing rather than on internally generated cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total available liquidity was USD 11,797 million at 30 September 2026, made up of cash and short-term investments of USD 8,287 million and undrawn facilities of USD 3,510 million, up from USD 9,233 million at 31 December 2025. Restricted cash and short-term investments of USD 555 million are excluded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C13; calculation C3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 59–60

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Principal of USD 29,321 million matures as USD 631 million in the remainder of 2026, USD 3,550 million in 2027, USD 7,861 million in 2028, USD 3,884 million in 2029, USD 2,729 million in 2030 and USD 10,666 million from 2031. 2028 is the largest single year and a further USD 10,666 million falls due from 2031, so access to refinancing matters more than near-term liquidity. A cargo receivables facility of USD 50 million inside the undrawn total expires in December 2026, letters of credit outstanding against the facilities are not stated for 30 September 2026, and the issuer states compliance with its loan-to-value, collateral coverage, minimum liquidity and debt service coverage covenants without giving a level or headroom for each instrument, so covenant capacity is not established here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer and supplier funding is large and sits outside debt: air traffic liability of USD 9,414 million, loyalty program liability of USD 11,514 million and fuel financing of USD 933 million at 30 September 2026. Fuel financing, USD 74 million at the 2024 year end, is classified as financing in the cash flow statement yet is not in Total Debt, so it is treated as working capital float and flagged. These balances support liquidity and operating cash flow while bookings and supplier terms hold, and they reverse if demand falls or if card processors impose holdback requirements, which the issuer says would reduce its liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Events after the FY2025 balance-sheet date are kept out of period figures: the first-quarter 2026 notice to redeem the 8.50% senior secured notes in full, which no longer appear in the 2026 debt table, and the 12 February 2026 amendment that replaced the 2025 AAdvantage term loan with new loans of the same principal at a lower margin. Both are already reflected in the 2026 balance sheets, so no pro forma adjustment is needed. After the 30 September 2026 balance-sheet date, the quarterly report states October 2026 exercises of purchase options on five Airbus A320 Family aircraft and a commitment to buy two Boeing 777-200ER aircraft in the fourth quarter, without amounts, so no net debt adjustment is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three multi-figure items change how the numbers are used. Debt is USD 29,635 million at carrying value and USD 29,321 million at principal, the difference being finance leases and issuance costs; cash is USD 8,287 million including short-term investments against USD 1,124 million for the balance sheet cash line, which moves net debt to EBITDA from 7.38x to 9.86x; and depreciation and amortization is USD 1,890 million on the income statement but USD 2,219 million on the cash flow statement for FY2025, which would lift FY2025 EBITDA by USD 329 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer states no EBITDA, so every leverage and coverage figure is built from statement lines and is only as reliable as that derivation; no adjusted EBITDA, add-back or EBITDA bridge is stated. Quarterly cash flow statements are cumulative from 1 January and print operating cash flow as one total, so cash flow quality in 2026 can be read only at the level of totals, and the fourth quarter of 2025 is constructed as FY2025 less nine months 2025 and labelled calculated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-03-31_aal_aal-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aal_aal-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8

fields.value: Unit cost excluding special items and fuel is stated on an annual definition (14.12 cents for FY2025) and unit cost excluding special items, fuel and profit sharing on a quarterly one (14.34 cents for Q3 2026), so the two series are kept apart. The 2024 year-end other accrued liabilities line is taken from the later annual report, which splits out fuel financing, and the earlier annual report's presentation is kept for FY2023.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High: The issuer states no EBITDA and no adjusted EBITDA in any of the five documents, so EBITDA is calculated as operating income plus depreciation and amortization from the income statement, every leverage and coverage figure depends on that calculation, and no adjusted ratio or EBITDA bridge is stated; a management reconciliation or an earnings release would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: Depreciation and amortization is USD 1,890 million on the FY2025 income statement but USD 2,219 million on the cash flow statement, so EBITDA would be USD 329 million higher on the second line; the income statement line is used and the issuer should say which it treats as depreciation and amortization for EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The first-quarter, first-half and nine-month 2026 cash flow statements print operating cash flow as one total, so the non-cash adjustments and working capital lines for those periods are not supplied, which restricts 2026 cash-flow quality analysis to totals; the earnings release cash flow tables would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: No source states a legal rank across the facilities: the debt note says only whether debt is secured, that the payroll support notes are senior unsecured obligations of the parent and that some equipment notes are junior to others on the same aircraft, and no executed document is supplied, so the debt stack states no rows, a senior secured subtotal cannot be built and structural priority is not established; the executed credit agreements and intercreditor terms would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The quarterly debt note prints principal, not carrying value, so finance leases carried within the balance-sheet debt lines (USD 660 million at 30 September 2026) are derived as the balance-sheet lines less the debt-note carrying value; the same derivation reproduces the annual lease note at 31 December 2025, and the finance lease balance in the quarterly report would confirm it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Instrument carrying values are not disclosed one by one, only an aggregate of unamortized discount, premium and issuance costs of USD 346 million at 30 September 2026, so the instruments register keeps principal and one financing cost row.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Income taxes paid is stated for FY2024 and FY2023 only and is not supplied for FY2025 or any 2026 period, so cash taxes are not tabulated for the latest periods; the supplemental cash flow information in the next annual report would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: The issuer does not split capital expenditures into maintenance and growth, so only total capital expenditures and aircraft purchase deposits are used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: No dividend, acquisition or share repurchase line appears in any cash flow statement, so none is tabulated and none is read as zero.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Fuel financing is printed as a dash on the 30 June 2026 balance sheet and is not a separate line in the FY2024 annual report for 31 December 2023; neither dash is read as zero.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: The FY2025 annual report shows fuel financing of USD 74 million separately at 31 December 2024, where the FY2024 annual report printed other accrued liabilities of USD 2,961 million, equal to the later 2,887 plus 74; the tables use the later presentation for FY2024 and the earlier one for FY2023.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: No fourth quarter is reported, so fourth-quarter 2025 revenue, EBITDA, net income and operating cash flow are constructed as FY2025 less nine months 2025 and labelled calculated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Letters of credit outstanding under the revolving facilities at 30 September 2026 are not stated in the quarterly report, which gives only maximum availability of USD 3,510 million; the annual report records no borrowings or letters of credit outstanding on the 2013 and 2014 revolving facilities at 31 December 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: A cargo receivables facility of USD 50 million, part of the USD 3,510 million undrawn total, is scheduled to expire in December 2026, within twelve months of the balance-sheet date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Unit cost excluding special items and fuel is stated for the annual reports (14.12 cents for FY2025 and 13.50 cents for FY2024) but the 2026 quarterly reports also exclude profit sharing (14.34 cents for Q3 2026), so the two series are not joined.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: The October 2026 aircraft purchase option exercises and the fourth-quarter 2026 commitment to buy two Boeing 777-200ER aircraft carry no stated amounts, so no post-balance-sheet net debt adjustment is stated and the events are flagged with their month only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: The nine-month cash flow statements print no separate line for net fuel financing and the first-quarter statements print none for sale-leaseback proceeds, so those two lines are not supplied for those columns although the other interim columns print them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: The group reports a single operating segment, so no segment revenue schedule is stated and no segment sum is shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This is the business, ownership and governance assessment of American Airlines Group Inc. as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway. It covers the group's business and operating model, ownership and control, the 2025 and 2026 financing transactions, dated issuer events and the governance and sponsor-behaviour assessment, drawn from five annual and quarterly filings and the source readiness assessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: American Airlines has no disclosed sponsor or controlling owner, so creditors face operating and structural risk rather than owner extraction: no dividends or buybacks were paid, but fuel-driven cost pressure and an increasingly secured, asset-backed debt stack drive the credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity of USD 11,797 million is the key protection against that pressure: fuel took 26.78% of nine-month operating costs with no hedges, and USD 5,985 million of secured debt depends on loyalty cash flows. Governance risk is medium because board, ownership and related-party detail was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C16; calculation C13; calculation C8; 10-K_2025-12-31_aal_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 264

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Owner-extraction risk is low but unverified: the shares are widely dispersed and no sponsor, parent or controlling holder is disclosed, yet board independence, holders above 5% and related-party terms sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied. Legal limits on foreign holders (24.9% of votes and 49.0% of equity) and a plan that dilutes any holder reaching 4.9% shape who can accumulate control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Shareholder behaviour has been creditor-aligned: no cash dividends or share repurchases were made in 2024 and 2025, the 2026 equity statements show only employee plan issuance equal to 0.35% of shares, and the only sizeable equity-linked cash outflow was USD 79 million to settle government warrants in 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Loyalty is a major cash engine and is already pledged to lenders: loyalty revenue was 13.81% of FY2025 revenue and partner cash payments were USD 6.2 billion in 2025, while USD 5,985 million of secured debt, 20.41% of principal, is repaid from those flows and secured on the programme's assets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C8; 10-K_2025-12-31_aal_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 167–169

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Costs, not demand, are the exposed side of the operating model: fuel was 26.78% of nine-month operating expenses against 20% in FY2025 with no hedges, each one-cent rise adds about USD 45 million to annual fuel cost, 86% of employees are unionised and regional capacity contracts commit USD 4,461 million of minimum-flying payments, so unit revenue growth of 10.9% did not stop operating income falling to USD 521 million from USD 1,015 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - New debt extended maturities and funded fleet renewal but raised both the amount and the secured share: principal rose by USD 727 million to USD 29,321 million, the secured share rose from 84.70% to 87.22%, and the only unsecured debt is the U.S. Treasury's USD 3,746 million of notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C7; calculation C10; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Funding flows from the operating subsidiary up to the parent: American Airlines, Inc. holds a net receivable from the parent of USD 12,512 million, which rose by USD 1,680 million in 2025, due in part to funding the USD 1.0 billion cash settlement of the convertible notes, and by USD 574 million in the nine months to September 2026, so the subsidiary's own creditors carry the parent's repayment risk on that balance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Litigation adds claims the filings do not size: the accident cases seek unspecified damages with trial set for 2027-04-12, the Northeast Alliance class action is at class certification, and the latest quarterly report no longer describes the accident cases that the second-quarter report said insurance covers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fleet renewal is a large claim on future cash: aircraft and engine commitments of USD 24,056 million remain, and 54.00% of the mainline fleet is owned, which keeps debt secured on aircraft and sustains the need for secured issuance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C5; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 64–66; 10-K_2025-12-31_aal_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 100

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the balance sheet: liquidity of USD 11,797 million, no dividends or buybacks, maturities moved out to 2031 and 2033, and revenue growth of 19.3% in the third quarter. Together they show creditors are protected by cash and market access rather than by sponsor support, and they leave little sign of value moving away from creditors apart from the intercompany funding of the parent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if fuel falls back toward the FY2025 average of USD 2.39 per gallon, if the proxy statement confirms no controlling holder and no conflicted related-party terms, and if the accident litigation is resolved within insurance. It would weaken if fuel stays near the third-quarter average of USD 3.85 per gallon, if distributions resume while the secured share keeps rising, or if executed documents show wide capacity to move assets outside the secured group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Board composition, independence, holders above 5%, executive pay and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the medium governance rating rests on behaviour shown in the financial statements and would move if the proxy shows a controlling holder or conflicted terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No executed debt documents were supplied, so the conclusion that no value has been moved away from creditors rests on reported transactions only, and capacity for restricted payments, liens and asset transfers is not assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The latest quarterly report omits the January 2025 Washington accident litigation that earlier reports described, so its status after 2026-06-10 is not established and the litigation conclusion uses the second-quarter report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The group reports one operating segment, so the revenue mix shows where revenue comes from but not profit by line, and the conclusion that loyalty is a major cash engine rests on revenue and cash payment amounts, not on a stated margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fleet, labour and loyalty facts are group figures while the principal subsidiary reports slightly different amounts (nine-month revenue of USD 46,979 million against USD 46,982 million for the group), so perimeter-sensitive conclusions use the group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No acquisition, merger, disposal or sponsor transaction appears in the five filings, so the transaction record is a funding one. In the nine months to September 2026 the group raised USD 5,933 million of long-term debt and repaid USD 5,347 million, and principal outstanding rose from USD 28,594 million at the 2025 year end to USD 29,321 million. No equity was issued for cash; the only new shares came from employee plans.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New secured aircraft and engine debt was the largest source: USD 127 million from the last of the 2025 aircraft trusts, USD 1,141 million from the May 2026 trusts, USD 567 million of engine certificates in June, USD 692 million so far from the USD 1.3 billion August trusts, USD 870 million of junior borrowings on aircraft already delivered and USD 705 million of floating-rate equipment loans. These sum to USD 4,102 million and match the roughly USD 4.1 billion the company reports. A further USD 633 million of the August proceeds sat in escrow at 2026-09-30 and is not counted as debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Bank debt was amended rather than replaced. In March 2026 the three revolving facilities were re-established with commitments of about USD 3.1 billion, undrawn, and their maturity moved from June 2029 to March 2031; in May 2026 about USD 1.1 billion of term loans due January 2027 were refinanced into term loans maturing May 2033 at SOFR plus 3.00%, with USD 703 million of incremental borrowings; and in February 2026 the margin on the 2025 AAdvantage term loan was cut to SOFR plus 2.75%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Repayments were funded from new debt and cash: USD 629 million of short-term term loan, USD 1.0 billion of 8.50% senior secured notes and USD 310 million of aircraft equipment notes were prepaid, alongside USD 2.8 billion of scheduled repayments. After these transactions the aircraft certificate balance is USD 9,332 million, the AAdvantage secured debt is USD 5,985 million, and the Treasury's notes of USD 3,746 million fall due in 2030 and 2031. One subsequent event in October 2026 added purchase options on five Airbus A320 Family aircraft to commitments the company intends to finance with cash and long-term debt.

fields.value: This is the fundamental credit assessment of American Airlines Group Inc. as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway. It synthesises the source readiness assessment, the financial foundation and the business and governance fact base with five annual and quarterly filings into a credit view, a downside scenario, ranked drivers and monitoring triggers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: American Airlines has a scaled network and USD 11,797 million of liquidity but a thin, eroding earnings base, so creditors rely on liquidity, customer-funded float and secured market access rather than cash earnings to service USD 29,321 million of principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt was 10.25x last-twelve-months EBITDA and EBITDA covered cash interest 1.81x, with free cash flow near zero after capital spending. The primary downside is persistent unhedged fuel cost against rising unit costs, and a 2028 maturity of USD 7,861 million that must be refinanced in secured markets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C7; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The earnings and leverage profile is weak and still deteriorating: EBITDA calculated from statement lines fell to USD 2,891 million over the last twelve months from USD 4,970 million in FY2023 while revenue grew 15.52%, so the EBITDA margin fell from 9.42% to 4.74% and total debt reached 10.25x EBITDA. Net debt fell 15.70% over the same period, which shows cash building and not earnings recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fuel is the transmission channel and it is unhedged: in the nine months to September 2026 fuel cost rose by USD 4,427 million, absorbing 69.74% of the USD 6,348 million revenue gain, and each ten cents per gallon adds about USD 450 million, or 15.57% of last-twelve-months EBITDA, so fuel at the third-quarter level erodes coverage faster than fares can reprice.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45, 69

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash generation does not fund investment from earnings: capital spending of USD 4,358 million was 1.51x EBITDA and free cash flow was negative USD 91 million, because operating cash flow of USD 4,267 million was lifted by USD 2,970 million of working capital and other items, and customer-funded float supplied 70.60% of nine-month operating cash flow, which reverses if bookings weaken.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C7; calculation C8; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is the genuine support but it is not unlimited: USD 11,797 million, including USD 3,510 million of undrawn facilities, covers 0.98x of the principal due through 2028 and 60.78% of that principal plus aircraft and engine commitments, so the debt service plan depends on continued financing as well as on cash on hand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing capacity is demonstrated but secured: in 2026 the company extended revolvers to 2031 and term loans to 2033 and raised USD 4,102 million of aircraft and engine debt, yet 87.22% of principal is secured, 52.24% sits in aircraft certificates and loyalty financing, and a USD 7,861 million maturity falls in 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C9; calculation C13; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy and governance are supportive but unverified: there is no sponsor, no dividend or buyback, and audited reporting, while American Airlines, Inc. holds a USD 12,512 million net receivable from the parent and board and ownership detail was not supplied, so governance risk stays medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business model supports revenue but not margin: loyalty is 13.81% of revenue and yield rose 12.1%, yet unit cost growth of 12.5% outran unit revenue growth of 10.9%, salaries rose USD 962 million, most employees are unionised and regional capacity contracts commit USD 4,461 million of minimum payments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C11; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48, 66; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Claims outside the debt figure add to the burden: operating lease liabilities of USD 6,639 million equal 22.40% of total debt, aircraft and engine commitments are USD 24,056 million, and the accident and antitrust litigation is not sized, so leverage understates the fixed claims on cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C17; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weak earnings reading is momentum and balance-sheet repair: third-quarter revenue grew 19.3%, yield rose 12.1% over nine months, liquidity rose to USD 11,797 million from USD 9,233 million at the 2025 year end, and net debt fell by USD 3,976 million since FY2023. If fuel prices fall back toward the FY2025 average of USD 2.39 per gallon while yield holds, EBITDA could recover quickly because most of the 2026 damage is the fuel price, not demand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–48; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if EBITDA cover of cash interest returns above the 2.28x of FY2023, if free cash flow turns positive without float growth, and if the 2028 maturity is refinanced early. It would weaken if fuel stays near the third-quarter average of USD 3.85 per gallon, if unit cost growth stays above unit revenue growth for another year, or if float reverses so that liquidity falls while the 2028 maturity approaches.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - EBITDA is built from statement lines because the issuer states none, and FY2025 depreciation differs by USD 329 million between the income statement and the cash flow statement, so every leverage and coverage conclusion is only as reliable as that derivation; if the same gap applied to the last twelve months, total debt would be 9.20x EBITDA rather than 10.25x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No executed debt documents, ratings or market prices were supplied, so covenant headroom, structural priority and legal capacity are not established and the view that refinancing stays open assumes no restriction on new secured debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer set or management guidance was supplied, so the business profile cannot be compared with other airlines and the outlook rests on filing trends, which limits the strength of the comparison with typical issuers in the sector.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interim cash flow statements print operating cash flow as one total, so the float share of operating cash flow is built from balance-sheet changes and could differ from the cash flow lines, which would change how much of the improvement is recurring.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Nothing dated after 2026-10-22 was supplied, so fuel, bookings and financing since the latest quarter are not reflected and the downside scenario is a sensitivity on reported trends, not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five strongest supports all work through cash availability rather than earnings. Liquidity of USD 11,797 million, with revolvers maturing in 2031 and term loans in 2033, gives the company time to absorb a fuel shock without a near-term maturity, which lowers the probability of a liquidity-driven default over the next two years even though it does not cover the 2028 wall alone. Loyalty brings partner cash of USD 6.2 billion in 2025 and 13.81% of revenue, which both supports unit revenue and gives lenders a pledgeable cash stream, although USD 5,985 million of secured debt already draws on it. Scale and network, with nine hubs and a domestic share of 70.89% of passenger revenue, spread demand across markets and let capacity and pricing respond to local conditions. Demonstrated access to asset-backed markets, with USD 4,102 million raised in nine months, lowers refinancing risk for as long as lenders accept aircraft collateral, whose values were not supplied. No dividends or buybacks keep cash in the business, which supports debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C13; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five weaknesses all work through thin earnings against fixed claims. Leverage of 10.25x and cash interest cover of 1.81x leave little room for a further earnings decline, so a modest fall in EBITDA moves both measures materially. Unhedged fuel and rising unit cost turn price shocks directly into lower EBITDA, as the 69.74% absorption of the 2026 revenue gain shows. Free cash flow of negative USD 91 million and dependence on float for 70.60% of nine-month operating cash flow mean the cash position is partly borrowed from customers and will shrink if bookings slow. The maturity profile puts USD 12,042 million of principal, 41.07% of the total, due by 2028, and the secured share of 87.22% limits the assets that can back new debt. Fixed commitments, namely USD 24,056 million of aircraft and engine purchases, USD 4,461 million of regional capacity payments, USD 6,639 million of operating leases and labour contracts that open in 2027, reduce cost flexibility when revenue falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C13; calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 64–66

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: American Airlines Group Inc. runs a major network carrier through American Airlines, Inc. and its regional subsidiaries, with nine hubs, service to more than 350 destinations and about 224 million passengers boarded in 2025. FY2025 revenue of USD 54,633 million was 83.48% passenger travel, 13.81% loyalty-related and 1.54% cargo, and 70.91% of passenger revenue was domestic, so cash flow comes mainly from advance ticket sales across a broad network and from partner payments for loyalty miles.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C20; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business model supports cash visibility but not earnings stability. Customers and loyalty members had advanced USD 20,928 million at 30 September 2026, which funds working capital and cushions the quarter-to-quarter swings, while the fleet, labour and regional capacity commitments are fixed, so a drop in demand or a rise in fuel falls straight through to EBITDA and to the cash available for the USD 29,321 million of principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C8; calculation C17; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company is widely held with no disclosed sponsor or controlling holder, so the risks that matter are cash leakage between group entities and the ranking of lenders, not sponsor extraction. American Airlines, Inc. is the main borrower of secured debt, American Airlines Group Inc. guarantees the senior secured notes and the loyalty financing, the parent's own debt is the USD 3,746 million of Treasury notes guaranteed by the subsidiaries, and American Airlines, Inc. holds a USD 12,512 million net receivable from the parent, which grew when the subsidiary funded the parent's USD 1.0 billion cash settlement of convertible notes in 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy has been supportive: no dividends or buybacks in 2024 and 2025, voluntary prepayment of the highest-coupon secured notes, and 2026 refinancings that extended maturities. Ownership restrictions on foreign holders and a tax benefit plan to October 2027 protect USD 11.9 billion of federal tax losses and limit concentrated accumulation. The legal rank of each facility and the capacity of the debt documents to permit asset transfers were not supplied, so structural priority is not established here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is driven by yield more than volume: over nine months 2026 capacity grew 4.3% and traffic 2.8%, load factor fell 1.2 percentage points and yield rose 12.1%, which lifted total unit revenue 10.9% and third-quarter revenue 19.3%. Revenue is discretionary, cyclical and seasonal, with a summer peak, and it is exposed to fuel, the economy and competition from network, low-cost and ultra-low-cost carriers that match fares market by market.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C11; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–48; 10-K_2025-12-31_aal_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is real but partial: the 2026 revenue gain of USD 6,348 million exceeded the USD 4,427 million fuel increase, but fuel took 69.74% of the gain and other costs rose USD 2,415 million, so operating income still fell USD 494 million, and the loyalty program adds a second revenue stream of partner payments that does not depend on seats flown. No customer concentration is disclosed, and the largest partner flows are given only in aggregate, so concentration risk in the co-brand card relationships is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The cost base is mostly fixed or externally set: fuel was 26.78% of nine-month operating expenses with no hedge, salaries, wages and benefits rose 7.36% to USD 14,027 million, about 86% of employees are unionised with the pilot and mechanic contracts opening in 2027, and regional capacity contracts commit USD 4,461 million of minimum payments whatever the load factor. Margins can be defended only through fares and capacity, and in 2026 unit cost growth of 12.5% exceeded unit revenue growth of 10.9%, which cut the EBITDA margin to 4.74% over the last twelve months from 9.42% in FY2023.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C11; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 47–48, 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_aal_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost flexibility sits in capacity and in the timing of aircraft deliveries, not in the cost lines. Management states that it is managing costs and reengineering the business, but the filings give no quantified savings, so the effect of those levers on margin is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending of USD 4,358 million over the last twelve months was 1.51x EBITDA, and the issuer does not split it into maintenance and growth. Operating cash flow of USD 4,267 million was 147.60% of EBITDA only because working capital and other items added USD 2,970 million after cash interest of USD 1,594 million, and free cash flow of negative USD 91 million was negative 3.15% of EBITDA, so earnings alone do not cover interest and investment together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Conversion depends on float and on financing: air traffic and loyalty liabilities rose USD 3,206 million in nine months, 70.60% of operating cash flow, and the company raised secured debt to pre-fund investment, with cash and short-term investments up USD 2,451 million against a USD 727 million rise in principal. Float reverses if bookings fall, and card processors can hold back cash if the financial position worsens, which would reduce liquidity at the moment it is needed. Cash taxes are low because of federal tax losses of USD 11.9 billion, but cash taxes for 2025 and 2026 are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C8; calculation C16; 10-K_2025-12-31_aal_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 62

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and sets fares: on most domestic nonstop routes the company faces other network carriers and low-cost and ultra-low-cost carriers, and price cuts are matched quickly, so a fuel-driven cost increase can only be recovered if rivals also raise fares, which limits how much fuel cost fares can recover; in 2026 fuel took 69.74% of the revenue gain. Entry is limited by gates, slots, aircraft supply and capital, but ultra-low-cost carriers and long-range narrowbody entry increase competition on international routes, so entry affects yield more than market share.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Substitutes matter on shorter segments, where ground and rail compete, and in discretionary travel, where customers can defer trips. Buyer power is high because fares are transparent and a significant share of tickets is sold through third-party distributors that charge more than direct channels, although the loyalty program and co-brand cards raise switching costs. Supplier power is concentrated: aircraft come from a few manufacturers with long lead times, fuel is bought at market prices, and unions represent most employees, so input costs are largely outside management control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Macro and regulatory factors are a primary driver of credit quality because they move fuel and demand. Oil and gas price volatility from conflict and trade policy drives the fuel price, which ranged from about USD 1.86 to about USD 4.78 per gallon in the first nine months of 2026, and a temporary U.S. Government shutdown cut fourth-quarter 2025 revenue. A 100 basis point rise in rates would raise interest expense on variable-rate debt by about USD 150 million and interest income by about USD 80 million, a net USD 70 million cost, so rate risk is secondary to fuel. Regulation by transportation and aviation authorities, foreign ownership limits and antitrust litigation shape capacity and cost but do not change the base view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths that support credit are the liquidity of USD 11,797 million, the loyalty cash stream, network scale and the absence of shareholder distributions. Weaknesses that constrain credit are 10.25x leverage, 1.81x interest cover, unhedged fuel and negative free cash flow. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are a fall in fuel prices with yields holding, the change of co-brand card issuer in 2026, whose financial effect is not quantified in the filings, fleet renewal that lowers unit fuel burn, and early refinancing of the 2028 maturity. Threats that could weaken it are fuel above the third-quarter level, labour contract openings in 2027, an unsized accident litigation with trial set for April 2027, and a reversal of customer float.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and diversification are the strongest dimensions: revenue of USD 54,633 million, nine hubs, a domestic share of 70.91% and a growing international share spread demand and give pricing options. Competitive advantage rests on the network, alliances and the loyalty program, which keep yield above unit cost but not by enough to protect margin. Cost and capex flexibility, margin stability and free cash flow stability are the weakest dimensions, as the 4.74% EBITDA margin, 1.51x capital spending to EBITDA and negative free cash flow show.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C7; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ability to refinance and liquidity are supportive but depend on continued secured financing, since liquidity covers 0.98x of principal due through 2028 and 87.22% of principal is already secured. Financial policy and governance are supportive in behaviour but incomplete in evidence. The trend is a thinner earnings base each year since FY2023 with cash and liquidity building through new debt, and the missing datapoints are an issuer-stated EBITDA, covenant levels and headroom, legal rank, ratings and peer comparisons.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C10; calculation C13; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the company has tailwinds in yield strength, a new co-brand card issuer in 2026 whose financial effect is not quantified, fleet renewal, extended revolvers and term loans, and USD 11,797 million of liquidity. Headwinds are fuel at the third-quarter level, unit cost growth above unit revenue growth, USD 631 million of principal in the remainder of 2026, USD 3,550 million in 2027 and USD 7,861 million in 2028, a cargo receivables facility that expires in December 2026, pilot and mechanic contract negotiations in 2027 and the April 2027 accident trial. Management gave no earnings guidance in the filings, so the outlook rests on reported trends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C9; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 44–48, 65–66; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aal_aal-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the tailwinds are a younger fleet with lower fuel use per seat and a loyalty program that grows with card spending, and the headwinds are 2030 and 2031 Treasury note maturities of USD 3,746 million, a USD 10,666 million block of principal from 2031 and USD 24,056 million of aircraft and engine commitments that keep demanding secured financing. Sector headwinds are competition on international routes and regulatory and labour constraints; sector tailwinds are limited by the lack of peer or industry forecasts in the inputs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C9; calculation C17; 10-K_2025-12-31_aal_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is fuel staying near the third-quarter average of USD 3.85 per gallon through 2027 while yield gains fade as capacity grows. The first operational break is the unit margin: unit cost already grew 12.5% against unit revenue growth of 10.9%, so a stall in yield turns the narrowed spread negative, and with unhedged fuel each additional ten cents per gallon adds about USD 450 million of annual cost. The financial transmission is lower EBITDA from USD 2,891 million, interest cover below the 1.81x level, and free cash flow that is negative even before a float reversal, since EBITDA less cash interest less capital spending is already negative USD 3,061 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The liquidity and refinancing consequence follows the float: if bookings weaken, air traffic and loyalty liabilities of USD 20,928 million shrink and card processors may hold back cash, so liquidity of USD 11,797 million falls while USD 12,042 million of principal falls due through 2028 and USD 7,366 million of aircraft and engine commitments fall due in the same period. Management levers are the USD 3,510 million of undrawn facilities, deferral of aircraft deliveries, capacity cuts, asset-backed financing and fares; resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027, but leverage would rise and the 2028 maturity would need refinancing from a weaker position. The observable triggers are listed in the monitoring register: fuel above the nine-month high, coverage below its current level, liquidity below its current level and delay in financing the remaining aircraft certificate escrow. No default is assumed because the sources do not support one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C8; calculation C10; 10-K_2025-12-31_aal_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 59–61, 65–66

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, American Airlines Group Inc. presents an adequate business profile supported by network scale, the loyalty program and USD 11,797 million of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by thin earnings, 10.25x leverage and unhedged fuel exposure. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow is negative and depends on customer float. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on continued access to aircraft and loyalty-backed secured markets and on the stability of collateral values. The primary downside path is persistent high fuel cost against rising unit costs and a 2028 maturity of USD 7,861 million. Further analysis would require executed debt documents, covenant levels, ratings, a peer set and any management guidance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C10; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment completed. Top risk: unhedged fuel cost against a thin and eroding earnings base.
